## Lego Huge CES Announcement #lego #ces #tech #gadgets #2026 
URL: https://www.tiktok.com/@sabrina_ramonov/video/7593887760746908959

Lego just introduced its biggest change in years at CES 2026, a new interactive system  called Lego Smart Play, built around the smart brick. Lego Smart Play is built around three  parts, the smart brick, smart tags, and smart minifigures. The smart brick is a 2x4 Lego brick  with electronics inside, a processor, lights, a speaker, and an accelerometer that senses how  the brick is moved. Smart tags are special tiles that act like physical instructions.  When the brick detects a tag, it changes its behavior, triggering different sounds or light  patterns. Smart minifigures work the same way. Each one has an embedded tag, and when it's placed  near the brick, the brick reacts with character-specific sounds and responses. Everything  happens directly inside the toy. There's no app, no coding, and no speech, just physical interaction  driving digital feedback. The advantage is simplicity. Interactive play without setup  or devices. But the limitation is flexibility. You can't program it, and you're limited to the  behaviors Lego builds into each set. So the smart brick isn't about teaching coding.  It's about making classic Lego sets feel responsive through built-in intelligence.

It's the difference between a teacher grading your homework based on getting the correct answer versus grading your homework  and looking at your reasoning steps to arrive at the correct answer.  For example, let's take the prompt, what is 2 plus 2?  Models before O1 were trained with human feedback that basically said any answer that is 4 is correct.  But O1 is trained with human feedback that looks at the reasoning steps.  So it will only mark the answer as correct if the reasoning is correct.  2 plus 2 equals 4 because 2 is 1 plus 1.  So 2 plus 2 is 1 plus 1 plus 1 plus 1, that equals 4.  If the reasoning was wrong, even if the final answer is 4, that would not count as a correct answer.  That is the key difference in how O1 was trained and why it represents a significant difference from other open AI models.  Out of all the different ways to get to the answer 4, chat GPT O1 has received feedback on what is the correct reasoning versus what is the wrong reasoning.  That is why it's performing extremely well on benchmarks in fields where there's a clear yes or no answer.  You'll be disappointed, however, if you're trying to use O1 for creative tasks like content creation and writing.
